title: Macterm desktop widgets
description: The desktop widgets, in ~/.config/macterm/widgets/widgets.yaml. Macterm maintains this file automatically — rewriting it whenever a widget is added, moved, resized or removed, and on quit — and reads your edits at launch and before each of its own writes. An added entry becomes a widget; removing an entry removes its widget at the next launch.

widgets.description: The widgets, in creation order. Entries carry no id: Macterm matches them to its widgets by `name`, then by content, then by position.

name.description: Optional label, shown in Settings → Widgets. Naming an entry makes hand-edits unambiguous.

size.description: A size family — small (1×1 cells), medium (2×1), large (2×2), extra-large (4×2) — or any grid span as COLUMNSxROWS, e.g. "3x2". A cell is 164pt with a 16pt gap, the system widgets' own module. Defaults to Settings → Widgets' default size.

column.description: The grid column of the widget's top-left corner, counted from the screen's left edge (0 is the first). With `row`; omit both to place the widget in the middle of the screen.

row.description: The grid row of the widget's top-left corner, counted from the top of the screen (0 is the first, just under the menu bar).

display.description: The screen the widget is on, by its name as System Settings → Displays shows it. Omit for the primary display (the one with the menu bar); a name that matches no connected screen also means the primary display.

cwd.description: Where the widget's shell starts when it starts fresh (absolute or ~-prefixed). Omit for the home directory. Captured from the widget's live shell.

run.description: A command typed into the widget's shell whenever it starts fresh — when the widget is created, when its shell exits, and at a launch that finds its session gone (e.g. after a reboot). Captured from what the widget is running, the way a pinned tab's is; a widget sitting at its prompt keeps the command it had.
